Its former Rank under the old shrine classification system was that of a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度}}<ref name=":0">『[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1088244/1/532 明治神社誌料：府県郷社 上]』</ref>{{Sfn|Fujimi Village History Compilation Committee|1954|pp=1071-1072}}. The shrine building stands atop Mount Jūni.
== History ==
The exact origins are unknown, but it is said to have been established as the {{ill|satomiya|ja|里宮}} (village shrine) of {{ill|Daidō Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社 (前橋市富士見町赤城山)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtō Akagi Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtō Akagi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11635469}} and was venerated by the lords of {{ill|Maebashi Castle|de|Burg Maebashi|es|Castillo de Maebashi|fa|قلعه مائه‌باشی|fr|Château de Maebashi|ja|前橋城|zh|前橋城|qid=Q10898917|lt=Maebashi Castle}} as a guardian of the {{ill|kimon|ja|鬼門}} (demon gate) alongside the Ōtō Akagi Shrine{{Sfn|Fujimi Village History Compilation Committee|1954|pp=1071-1072}}. In Meiji 5 (1872), it was designated as a Gōsha (village shrine){{Sfn|Fujimi Village History Compilation Committee|1979|pp=1142-1143}}.
The enshrined deities are:

- {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q386563}}

Traces of a {{ill|tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室}} (pit-style stone chamber) and a circular arrangement of river stones remain within the shrine grounds, and the discovery of artifacts such as swords and {{ill|mimikazari|ja|耳環|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/mimikazari|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/mimikazari|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11647642}} (earrings) suggests the presence of a burial mound. This site is not registered in the Jōmō Burial Mound Survey{{Sfn|Fujimi Village History Compilation Committee|1954|p=665}}.

پریفیکچر|vi|Gunma|war|Gunma (prefektura)|wuu|群马县|zh|群馬縣|zh_classical|群馬縣|zh_min_nan|Gunma-koān|zh_yue|群馬縣|qid=Q129499|lt=Gunma Prefecture}}. It is also known as '''Kunimigatake'''{{Sfn|Fujimi Village History Compilation Committee|1954|p=471}} or '''Kunimigaoka'''{{Sfn|Fujimi Village History Compilation Committee|1979|p=1141}}, with an elevation of 300 meters{{Sfn|Fujimi Village History Compilation Committee|1954|pp=1071-1072}}. It is famous for azaleas and is mentioned in the local karuta game "Fujimi Karuta" with the line: "Azaleas of Akagi and Mount Jūni"{{Sfn|Fujimi Village History Compilation Committee|1954|pp=1071-1072}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fujimi Karuta Tour, Maebashi City, Gunma Prefecture |url=https://fujimimachi.jp/karuta/karuta_tu.html |website=fujimimachi.jp |access-date=2024-07-18}}</ref>.
The name is believed to derive from the worship of the mountain god {{ill|Jūnisho Shrine|ja|十二所神社}} (Ōyamatsumi) as "Jūninyō"{{Sfn|Fujimi Village History Compilation Committee|1954|p=1009}}. The Edo-period "{{ill|Maebashi Fudoki|ja|前橋風土記}}" states that the name originates from the worship of the Twelve Heavenly Deities at the mountain summit<ref>『[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1183477/1/34 前橋風土記]』</ref>. There is a legend that stones were quarried from Mount Jūni during the construction of Maebashi Castle{{Sfn|Fujimi Village History Compilation Committee|1954|p=1039}}.
At the summit is a stone {{ill|Kōshin-tō|ja|庚申塔}} established in the first year of Man'en (1860){{Sfn|Fujimi Village History Compilation Committee|1954|pp=1071-1072}}, and halfway up the mountain is a {{ill|Gorintō|en|Gorintō|qid=Q304906|lt=Gorintō}} called Kazefusama{{Sfn|Fujimi Village History Compilation Committee|1954|p=1015}}. To the southwest foot is a {{ill|Hayagriva (Buddhism)|en|Hayagriva (Buddhism)|qid=Q17004306|lt=Batō Kannon}}, which is said to be the remains of a {{ill|amateur kabuki|ja|地芝居|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/jishibai|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/jishibai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q11605564|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11605564}} (folk theater) stage{{Sfn|Fujimi Village History Compilation Committee|1954|p=1036}}.
On the southern slope lies a round burial mound, 35 meters in diameter, called the '''Hatsumuro Kofun''' (Jōmō Burial Mound Survey No. 7). It contains a {{ill|yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}}, but has been plundered{{Sfn|Fujimi Village History Compilation Committee|1954|p=665}}.
